newsitem.title: TURKEY: TURK UKI TO MEET 60 MLN MARK 97 SALE TARG.
newsitem.headline: TURK UKI TO MEET 60 MLN MARK 97 SALE TARG.

text.p: Turkish ready-to-wear producer UKI, Uluslararasi Konfeksiyon Imalat ve Ticaret A.S. will meet its 60-million-mark turnover target in 1997, based on early results, a senior company official said.

"The results of the first five months of 1997 and the orders for rest of the year show that we will meet our 60-million-mark total sales target this year," Turan Sarigulle, president of the company, told Reuters.
Uki's total sales was at 53.3 million marks in 1996, including 47.5 million marks of exports. The company aims to earn 50 million marks from exports this year.
France, Germany and Italy are the major export markets and Belarus and Russia are the main target markets of the company.
Shares of the company closed at 8,900 lira on the Istanbul Stock Exchange on Wednesday, when the market index firmed 0.97 percent, up slightly from Tuesday's 8,800.
The company increased its output to 1.1 million units in 1996 from a previous 1.05 million units and aims to raise it to 1.4 million units this year, with a capacity utilisation rate of 90 percent.
Sarigulle said stability of Uki's customer base in the European markets would help them to meet their turnover target.
"Our customers inform us at least six months ahead in case they plan to reduce their orders if they have to," he said.
"And this gives us enough time to find new substitute markets and customers to create new orders and demand for our excess production," he added.
"We will concentrate on the domestic market this year and aim to sell Turkish consumers more than we used to before," Sarigulle said.
The company recently introduced products under Italian Gian Alberto Caporale, French Bruno Saint Hilaire and German Cinque brands to the domestic market.
Sarigulle said Turkey's customs union deal with Europe which took effect in the beginnig of 1996, alerted Turkish textile producers to seek international brand licences.
"We knew that several of them would enter the Turkish market after the customs union deal went ahead and we decided to become partners with them to share the market slice together," he said.
The company produces trousers, jackets and coats for men with around 1,300 workers at its plant near Istanbul.
UKI reported 1.368 trillion lira turnover in the first quarter of 1997 against 815 billion in the same period of 1996 and its net profits rose to 210 billion lira from 124 billion.
